narration_overrides.1: Near Qasr El Einy in Cairo, I bought a microscope for myself. Getting it home to Qatar became another problem altogether, and I was determined to bring it anyway.
narration_overrides.2: The instrument was mine. I could examine a slide without a laboratory booking, return to it another morning, and follow questions that had not yet become formal research projects.

narration_overrides.1: I finished high school at sixteen. Hospital admissions had interrupted much of my final year, and my examination results cost me the medical-school path I had been preparing for.
narration_overrides.2: Chemistry came next. I learned to observe materials under a microscope and ask questions that experiments could answer. The illness did not wait for a convenient time to return.
narration_overrides.4: A week before I was due to travel to the United States, another attack led to an endoscopy and a course of glucocorticoids. I was already ill when treatment began.
